transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for meeting with me. And thank you to your sister for being here. I want to talk to you about what happened during your surgery today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay? You look really serious.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm afraid it isn't. During the procedure, I placed a surgical clip on the wrong structure. I am very sorry. This was my mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What? What does that even mean? Was it something important?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is shocking to hear. To be clear, I clipped a piece of tissue that should not have been clipped. Because of this, we had to perform an additional procedure right there in the operating room to fix it and remove the clip.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It did extend the time you were under anesthesia.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I can't believe this. I have two kids at home. I'm already terrified about how I'm going to manage them if I'm stuck in here. Now you're telling me you messed up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how overwhelming this is, especially with your children waiting for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have two jobs. I don't have a "recovery period" that lasts weeks. My kids have no one else to watch them if I'm not okay. Am I even going to be able to walk tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels like everything is piling up right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is no excuse for it. I simply made a mistake in the placement. I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel sick. I trusted you. I'm just... I'm so scared that I'm not going to be okay for my girls.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel frightened. This is a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: In terms of the immediate physical result, the correction was successful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what about the recovery? Does this change when I can go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will monitor you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure yet. We'll have to see how you feel.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: See how I feel? I need to know. I have to call my boss. I have to tell my childcare provider. I can't just "see."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that's frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the nurses will be coming in and out. We'll just keep an eye on the incision site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? When do I get to see my kids?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just keep checking in.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a very difficult moment for both of you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I can't be here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you want to get back to your family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably just handle it during the usual rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel like I can trust anyone here right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that trust has been broken. I am truly sorry for the distress and the error I caused.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no comprehension checks performed.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language, took full personal responsibility, and maintained accountability throughout the encounter.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions ('overwhelming', 'frightened') and referenced the patient's specific concerns regarding her children.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('we'll see', 'keep checking in', 'handle it during rounds') with no timelines, patient role, or prevention plan.
